property_summary: Calls to withdrawAll by any address other than the contract's owner always revert.
If the provided caller is not the current owner, then withdrawAll must revert when invoked by a non-owner (i.e. caller == c.owner() || reverted).

For every call to sendMoney(target, value, data) when msg.sender is the contract owner, the reference contract preserves that owner can withdraw the same balance afterwards (i.e., onlyOwner allows owner to withdrawAll), whereas the mutant inverts onlyOwner and can let a non-owner perform sendMoney and thereby change contract balance such that owner withdrawAll no longer equals the reference behavior for some inputs.

For any caller and value, when the contract's owner calls sendMoney(...) the call succeeds and the owner remains able to withdraw the same contract balance afterward; the mutant inverts onlyOwner allowing non-owners to call sendMoney and so can change contract balance in a way that makes the owner's withdraw behavior differ.

For all callers and values, if the contract owner calls sendMoney(target, value, data) (i.e. msg.sender == owner) the call succeeds and after it the owner can still withdraw the full contract balance via withdrawAll; the mutant inverts the onlyOwner check so owner cannot call sendMoney, allowing a non-owner attacker to call sendMoney and change contract balance so the owner's withdrawAll outcome can differ.

For every caller and amount, if the contract owner calls sendMoney(target, value, data) then the call will succeed (not revert) and afterwards the owner can still withdraw the same contract balance via withdrawAll; the mutant inverts onlyOwner so the owner cannot call sendMoney, allowing a non-owner attacker to call sendMoney and change contract balance such that the owner's ability to withdrawAll can differ (causing the property to fail for some inputs).

For every caller `actor` and amount `value` such that `actor` is the contract owner, calling sendMoney(target, value, data) from owner is allowed by the correct contract and will not prevent the owner from later withdrawing the contract's remaining balance via withdrawAll; the mutant inverts onlyOwner and forbids the owner, allowing non-owners to call sendMoney and thus can make the owner's withdrawAll outcome differ for some fuzzed inputs.

For any callee address that may reject payments (i.e., revert on receive/fallback), the reference implementation always routes withdrawals through withdraw(uint) so withdrawAll will revert when the transfer to owner would fail via withdraw(), whereas the mutated version does a direct transfer and will instead revert or behave differently when the owner's receiving fallback reverts — therefore the general rule: withdrawAll either consistently uses withdraw() so its success/failure matches withdraw(uint) behavior for all inputs; the mutant breaks this by bypassing withdraw(uint) and changing observable success/revert for some adversarial owner addresses.

For every owner address that may reject incoming payments (i.e. its payable fallback/receive reverts), the reference C's withdrawAll call always forwards through withdraw(uint) so its success/revert behavior matches withdraw(uint) (i.e. withdrawAll reverts when the owner cannot receive); the mutant that replaces that call with a direct transfer to msg.sender can change the success/revert observable outcome for such adversarial owner contracts, violating this consistency.

For every possible owner contract that may reject or re-enter on receiving funds, calling withdrawAll() on the correct contract delegates to withdraw(uint) so its success/revert behavior and resulting address(c).balance are consistent with withdraw(uint); the mutant that directly transfers address(this).balance to msg.sender can change whether the call succeeds (or how balance changes) for some adversarial owner contracts, breaking that consistency.

For every owner contract that may revert when receiving Ether, the reference C always routes withdrawAll() through withdraw(uint) so withdrawAll() reverts (and leaves contract balance unchanged) exactly when a direct attempt to send Ether to the owner via withdraw(uint) would revert; the mutant bypasses withdraw(uint) and can change whether withdrawAll() succeeds for some adversarial owner, so the rule (withdrawAll either succeeds and empties the contract or reverts and leaves balance unchanged in the same way withdraw(uint) would) is violated by the mutant for some owner that reverts on receive.

For every possible recipient behavior, calling withdrawAll() on the correct contract always routes through withdraw(uint) so its observable success (no revert) and resulting contract balance match what withdraw(uint) would produce; the mutant bypasses withdraw(uint) and can cause withdrawAll() to succeed or fail differently (and thus leave a different contract balance) for some adversarial recipient.

For every caller and any balance, only the contract owner can successfully withdraw the contract's balance via withdrawAll; the mutant removes the onlyOwner check so some non-owner caller can make withdrawAll succeed, violating this rule.

For every caller and any contract balance, only the deployer (owner) can successfully make the contract's balance drop to zero via withdrawAll; the mutant allows some non-owner caller to succeed, violating this rule.

For every caller and for every nonzero contract balance, only the deployer (owner) can successfully withdraw the entire contract balance via withdrawAll; the mutant removing onlyOwner allows some non-owner caller to succeed, violating this rule.

In the reference, withdrawAll can only be successfully invoked by the owner (calls by non-owners revert), whereas the mutant removes that restriction allowing some non-owner caller to succeed; the property: for every caller address, calling withdrawAll either succeeds only when the caller is the owner — i.e., non-owners cannot make withdrawAll succeed.

For every caller address and any initial contract balance funded via sendMoney to a helper that forwards funds, calling withdrawAll succeeds iff the caller is the owner (i.e., only the owner can make withdrawAll succeed when the contract holds nonzero balance); the mutant removes that owner restriction so some non-owner caller can make withdrawAll succeed.
